name: Salesmate
tagline: Track contacts and deals and send low-volume permissioned email through a user provider

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 5,000 Smart Flow execution credits/user/month; full email sync, web forms and standard reports
tiers.notes: Live page defaulted to annual billing; its month-to-month USD amount was not exposed in the official page text checked.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 10,000 Smart Flow credits/user/month; sequences, team inbox, SSO and custom reports
tiers.notes: Live page defaulted to annual billing; its month-to-month USD amount was not exposed in the official page text checked.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 15,000 Smart Flow credits/user/month; custom modules, surveys, SLA tools, power dialer and voicemail drop
tiers.notes: Live page defaulted to annual billing; its month-to-month USD amount was not exposed in the official page text checked.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom limits; includes 1 dedicated IP, audit logs, dedicated account manager and 24x7 support
tiers.notes: Custom subscription price; mandatory enterprise onboarding packages start at $1,999.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier (15-day trial with unlimited invited users; monthly or annual plan required afterward)
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual page says save up to 20%); fees charged in advance and non-refundable
pricing.hiddenCosts: Calling/SMS requires a number starting at $1.10/month plus prepaid usage credits. Extra Smart Flow credits, dedicated IP and AI-agent credits cost extra; Enterprise onboarding starts at $1,999; taxes, bank and transaction charges are borne by the buyer.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Salesmate, track contacts and deals and send low-volume permissioned email through a user provider. The hard boundary is built-in calling, texting, sequences, automations, and sales integrations, plus integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in.
coreLoopDIY: Manage contacts, companies, and deals, move opportunities through a pipeline, log interactions, send low-volume permissioned email through a user provider, and surface the next action.
whatYouLose: built-in calling, texting, sequences, automations, and sales integrations
moatNotes: integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in
ongoingBurden: deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Salesmate because CRM value compounds as the system becomes the shared memory of every customer interaction and embeds itself in the rest of the stack. The recurring cost buys deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Twenty
priorArt.desc: Active open-source modern CRM with extensible data models.

alternatives.name: EspoCRM
alternatives.desc: A traditional CRM that actually lets you change the data model; polished enough, but still your server.

facts.install: Docker Compose or upload the PHP package and run the web installer
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in a self-hosted MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; uploaded files in server/Docker volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: EspoCRM does not provide Salesmate’s polished built-in calling, email sequences, and workflow automation out of the box.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server, database, domain/TLS setup, and ongoing upgrades/backups

alternatives.name: Frappe CRM
alternatives.desc: A clean leads-and-deals board with notes, tasks and email; Frappe underneath means a real server, not a toy.

facts.install: One-click Frappe Cloud signup or the official Python easy-install deployment script on your server
facts.dataFormat: CRM DocType records and attachments in the Frappe site database/files, on Frappe Cloud or the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe CRM offers mailbox-linked deal work but lacks Salesmate’s integrated calling, sequences, and mature sales automation.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use means self-hosting; the official production script still needs a Linux server, DNS, and command-line access

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A real two-seat CRM for free; 1,000 contacts is where the upsell starts counting.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optionally connect/import email, calendar, and contacts
facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM customer records stored and processed on HubSpot's cloud servers, with regional hosting options and exports
facts.gapVsPaid: HubSpot Free sharply limits the sequences, calling, and automation that make Salesmate more than a contact-and-deal database.

alternatives.name: SuiteCRM
alternatives.desc: The old-school full-fat CRM: every module you remember, plus the server you now own.

facts.install: Download the release and run the web/CLI installer on a LAMP server; paid managed hosting is optional
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in MySQL/MariaDB or MSSQL and attachments on the chosen server/object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: SuiteCRM can support email campaigns, but the experience is far less polished and immediate than Salesmate’s cloud calling and sales workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a correctly configured PHP web server and database, then ongoing backups, upgrades, and security maintenance

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.desc: A modern pipeline CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync; the subscription becomes a Compose file.

facts.install: Hosted cloud signup or official one-line/Docker Compose self-host install
facts.dataFormat: CRM records and configuration in PostgreSQL; files in local storage or S3-compatible object storage on the selected host
facts.gapVsPaid: Twenty synchronizes mailboxes but does not yet match Salesmate’s outbound sequences, telephony, and ready-made automation.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use requires Docker, at least 2 GB RAM, PostgreSQL-backed containers, secrets, and domain/TLS configuration

alternatives.name: Zoho CRM Free
alternatives.desc: Contacts, deals, and 150 emails a day for three users; enough for permissioned, low-volume selling.

facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM service data stored on Zoho's cloud servers; Zoho states users can access, export, and delete service data
facts.gapVsPaid: Zoho CRM Free covers low-volume email but its automation, mass-email, and calling capabilities are much more restricted than Salesmate’s.

alternatives.name: Freshsales Free
alternatives.desc: A three-user CRM with built-in email and one pipeline; sequences live in paid land.

facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM records and uploaded files stored in Freshworks' cloud; account data can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: Freshsales Free supplies a basic pipeline and email but leaves sequences and richer workflow automation to paid plans.

alternatives.name: Odoo CRM One App Free
alternatives.desc: A hosted pipeline with email activities for unlimited users; mass-mail cleverness is elsewhere.

facts.install: Hosted Odoo Online signup with CRM selected as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: Structured Odoo records in an Odoo-hosted customer database; records can be exported from list views
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo’s one-app-free CRM does not include the separate email-marketing and marketing-automation apps needed to approach Salesmate’s outreach workflow.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a personal or very small-team CRM DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Salesmate in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage contacts, companies, and deals, move opportunities through a pipeline, log interactions, send low-volume permissioned email through a user provider, and surface the next action.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create contacts, companies, opportunities, notes, tasks, and configurable pipeline stages.
Add fast global search, duplicate detection, merge, CSV import, and CSV export.
Provide a chronological interaction timeline with manual email and meeting logging.
Implement saved views, filters, owner assignment, and a next-action dashboard.
Add role-based access, an immutable activity log, backups, and a recovery command.
Seed a realistic demo workspace and document field mapping for imports.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out automatic mailbox ingestion.
Deliberately leave out commercial enrichment databases.
Deliberately leave out enterprise forecasting, integrations, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
